Acceptable Year of the Lord
ak-SEP-tuh-buhl yeer uhv thuh lord
noun
From Isaiah 61:2, quoted by Christ in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:19); the year of the Lord’s favour.

See also: Acceptable Year of the LORD

📖 Biblical Definition

The acceptable year of the Lord is the year of God’s favour proclaimed in the gospel, the phrase of Isaiah which the Lord Jesus read in the synagogue at Nazareth and applied to Himself: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord. Closing the book, He declared, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears. The phrase echoes the year of jubilee, when debts were released, slaves set free, and inheritances restored; in Christ the true jubilee is come, the day of salvation, the time accepted in which God receives sinners through His Son. Notably the Lord stopped His reading before the words the day of vengeance of our God, for His first coming opened the era of grace; the day of vengeance awaits His return. The dictionary honors the acceptable year of the Lord as the gospel age itself, the open door of mercy now proclaimed to the captives and the bruised, and warns that this accepted time is also a limited time: behold, now is the accepted year; today, if ye will hear His voice, harden not your hearts.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The year of God’s favour proclaimed in the gospel, the jubilee fulfilled in Christ, who read Isaiah 61 at Nazareth and declared it fulfilled that day.

ACCEPTABLE YEAR OF THE LORD, the year of God’s favour in the gospel.

From Isaiah 61, read by Christ in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luk 4:19).

He declared, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

Echoes the jubilee: debts released, captives freed, inheritance restored.

He stopped before the day of vengeance, which awaits His return.

📖 Key Scripture

Luk 4:19 — "To preach the acceptable year of the Lord."

Luk 4:21 — "And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears."

Isa 61:2 — "To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;"

2Co 6:2 — "(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The acceptable year is read as a program of merely social liberation; Scripture proclaims the gospel jubilee of salvation in Christ, an open but limited day of grace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The chief corruption is the reduction of the acceptable year to a program of social and economic liberation only, as if Christ’s mission at Nazareth were chiefly political. The jubilee imagery is real—release, liberty, restoration—but its fulfilment in Christ is the deliverance of sinners from the bondage of sin and death, the healing of the brokenhearted, and the opening of the prison of guilt. To flatten the acceptable year into mere social reform is to miss the salvation it proclaims.

The principle to recover is twofold. First, the acceptable year is the gospel age itself, the open door of mercy: Christ stopped His reading before the day of vengeance (Isa 61:2), for His first coming opened the era of grace, and the vengeance awaits His return. Second, the accepted time is a limited time. Paul presses the urgency: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). The acceptable year is open today, but it will close; the gospel call is therefore, Today, if ye will hear His voice, harden not your hearts.
